articles.title: Nations League roundup: Devenny’s divine strike lifts Northern Ireland to top tier
articles.summary: Haaland’s late penalty grabs Norway last-eight spot. Parrott penalties help Republic of Ireland secure playoff. A wonder strike from Justin Devenny earned Northern Ireland top spot in Nations League Group B2 and promotion to the top tier of the competition.
body: Northern Ireland had fallen 1-0 behind after a 35th-minute goal from the striker Barnabas Varga, who slotted home when one-on-one with the goalkeeper Pierce Charles after a defensive mix-up. The goal ended Northern Ireland’s proud record of not having conceded in this campaign and also sent Hungary to the top of the group in the live standings.

But moments after Isaac Price had hit the post for O’Neill’s young outfit, Devenny smashed the ball into the top left-hand corner in the 65th minute to restore Northern Ireland’s one-point advantage as group leaders. As time ticked down, Hungary pushed forward in increasing desperation – with Rajmund Toth firing over late on – but Northern Ireland dug in with the defensive resilience which has been the cornerstone of their campaign.

“It’s a great feeling for us,” said O’Neill, who had to watch the game from the stands as he served a touchline ban. “We set out when we came into this level of the competition to first of all try and stay and we knew to be in the top two positions would help us.

articles.title: Former world boxing champion Jorge Linares faces deportation after ICE arrest
articles.summary: Venezuelan boxer, 41, held at El Paso facility. Lawyers say three-weight champion is in US legally. ICE alleges Linares overstayed authorized visit. Former world boxing champion Jorge Linares has been detained by US immigration authorities in Texas, despite his lawyers insisting the retired…
body: Linares is being held at the El Paso Processing Center, according to federal detention records reviewed by the San Antonio Express-News. US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) said he was arrested at El Paso International Airport on Sunday after overstaying the period he was authorized to remain in the country.
The 41-year-old boxing great, who captured titles across three weight classes from featherweight to lightweight, first disclosed his detention in a post on X on Sunday.
“ICE has me at the Texas border crossing. This is crazy,” Linares wrote in Spanish. He has not posted publicly since.

ICE spokeswoman Leticia Zamarripa said Linares was arrested by US Border Patrol agents and ICE officers on 15 November after entering the United States on 26 October 2023 with permission to remain for a temporary period.

articles.title: Belief and bench help Northern Ireland scale new heights as promotion secured
articles.summary: Manager Michael O'Neill hails the belief shown by his side after they come from behind against Hungary to earn the draw required for promotion to Nations League A.
body: After going 500 minutes without conceding a goal, Northern Ireland could be forgiven for having to make adjustments to play from behind.

Having travelled to Budapest knowing a point against Hungary would be enough to top Nations League B2, Barnabas Varga's strike after 35 minutes for the hosts at the Puskas Arena altered the picture and, for the first time in the campaign, left Michael O'Neill's side having to chase a game.

Their response to the deficit - on the pitch, from the bench and high in the stands where their suspended manager was watching the game - displayed the best characteristics of a side who had not won at this level before this unbeaten campaign.

While the point from a 1-1 draw in Budapest will be long remembered for Justin Devenny's brilliant equaliser and the scenes of celebration that greeted promotion to the competition's top tier for the first time, it was beyond the highlights and headlines that O'Neill saw the emerging qualities of his side.

articles.summary: One way or another, Portugal’s No 7 shirt has caused quite the commotion in recent weeks and months, if not years. Perhaps it was inevitable, then, that the first win of the post-Cristiano Ronaldo era would come courtesy of the player wearing the updated jersey, one with a cross through the number…
body: For Wales, a Nations League relegation playoff double-header awaits in March, with Slovenia, Hungary, Republic of Ireland or Bosnia and Herzegovina – who knocked them out of World Cup qualifying this year – all potential opponents in Friday’s draw in Switzerland. Afterwards Craig Bellamy stressed the importance of keeping elite company to accelerate improvement but reiterated that he will not be in the job beyond Euro 2028, after which his contract expires.

“If we want to develop as a ­football nation and continue to move ­forward, we have to be playing against the best teams,” Bellamy said. “It’s only going to improve us. I was the best manager going in [Group] B, finished top … how good am I? Now I’m in [Group] A, we’ve played quite well, but I’m crap. It’s about playing the best teams, that’s how we’re going to get better. I won’t be here for the next Nations League, I won’t be the manager then, so I’m doing it for the next one.”

articles.title: ‘Heads should roll’: owner of Melbourne Cup horse found dumped in skip bin demands investigation
articles.summary: Stuart Ramsey says it is a ‘bloody disgrace’ the gelding was left in waste container while awaiting burial. Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast.
body: So You Are’s owner-breeder has demanded a full investigation after the Melbourne Cup runner’s body was found in a skip at a Sydney tip, insisting “heads have got to roll”.
Stuart Ramsey says it is a “bloody disgrace” that the gelding was left in the skip bin while awaiting burial at Sydney’s Cleanaway Lucas Heights resource recovery centre.
The grisly sight was uncovered by a Sydney man, with online footage outraging the racing industry and anti-horse racing activists alike.
The New South Wales premier, Chris Minns, said on Wednesday that the matter “obviously needs to be investigated” but “we expect to get to the bottom of it”.

articles.title: Republic of Ireland talisman Parrott caps dream year with two more goals
articles.summary: Republic of Ireland striker Troy Parrott reflects on a transformative 12 months for both club and country after scoring a double in the win against Kosovo.
body: A year and a day on from his hat-trick in Budapest which helped Republic of Ireland snatch a dramatic 3-2 win over Hungary to make the World Cup play-offs, Troy Parrott scored another two big goals to help the Irish to a 3-0 win over Kosovo in the Nations League.

His two penalties set Heimir Hallgrimsson's side on their way to a much-needed victory as they secured second spot in Group B3 - which brings with it a place in pot two for the Euro 2028 qualifying draw and a Nations League play-off with the chance to go up to League A for the first time.
The two strikes brought Parrott's tally for his country up to 17 in 43 caps.
Twelve of those goals have come in his past nine competitive appearances, with six in his past three games at the Aviva Stadium.

articles.title: Senegal and Morocco lead Afcon qualifiers but Tunisia protest
articles.summary: Senegal, Cameroon and Morocco qualify for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations, but Nigeria are in trouble, and struggling Tunisia fail with an impassioned penalty protest.
body: Senegal became the first side to qualify for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations before Cameroon and Morocco were among five others to join them with two games to spare - but there was penalty drama in Tripoli.
Tunisia, who have appeared at a record 17 consecutive editions of Afcon, are at risk of missing out after a contentious 1-1 draw against Libya.
Libya's penalty equaliser just before half-time followed protest scenes lasting over five minutes as players and staff from the Carthage Eagles challenged the decision.

The video assistant referee system is not used in Afcon qualifying, and Tunisia's remonstrating with the fourth official on the touchline ultimately only served to delay the spot-kick, which Ezoo El Mariamy, the player who was adjudged to have been fouled, converted.

articles.summary: England have topped their group in the Nations League after an incredible win over Spain - but who will they play in the last eight in March?
body: England's win over Spain in Madrid means they have finished top of the group.

That matters as the winners of the Nations League tier A groups are seeded for the quarter-final draw. They will play teams which have finished runners-up in other groups. They will also play the second leg of their quarter-final at home.
Belgium finished runners-up in Group A1, so they are a potential last-eight opponent for England.
Netherlands are another potential opponent as they finished second in Group A2 following their 5-0 loss to Germany, who topped the group.

body: Barnabas Varga ended Northern Ireland's proud record of not having conceded in this campaign when he fired the hosts in front after 35 minutes - a goal that also sent Hungary to the top of the group.

But moments after Isaac Price had hit the post for Michael O'Neill's young side, Devenny smashed the ball into the top left-hand corner in the 65th minute to restore Northern Ireland's one-point advantage as group leaders.

The visitors were on the back foot for much of the first half, with Hungary captain Dominik Szoboszlai hitting the post, but O'Neill, serving a touchline ban in the stands as former captain Steven Davis led things from the touchline, orchestrated key substitutions.

Northern Ireland started with Patrick Kelly in place of the suspended Jamie Donley up front but brought on Josh Magennis at half-time before Kieran Morrison and Brodie Spencer soon followed to help the visitors become a much greater threat going forward.

articles.summary: Troy Parrott fired the Republic of Ireland into a Nations League play-off berth with two penalties in their 3-0 victory over 10-man Kosovo at the Aviva Stadium in Dublin.
body: The result ensured the Republic finished runners-up in group B3, and also propelled the Euro 2028 co-hosts into a coveted pot-two seeding for next month's qualifying draw for that competition.
Tuesday night's contest turned on its head in the 26th minute, when Kreshnik Hajrizi was sent off for handling the ball off the line, and Parrott took advantage with a top-corner finish.

The Real Betis striker doubled the Republic's lead from the spot five minutes after the restart, and Jack Moylan added a 75th-minute cushion to keep alive the hosts' hopes of booking a place in League A for the first time through the March play-off.
Heimir Hallgrimsson's lone change from Saturday's defeat to group winners Austria was the insertion of John Egan into the line-up, replacing injured captain Nathan Collins.

articles.title: Paul McGinley Warns DP World Tour Regulars Face挤压 From LIV Returnees
articles.summary: Former European Ryder Cup captain Paul McGinley has issued a blunt assessment regarding the recent influx of LIV Golf players back onto the DP World Tour, including Bryson DeChambeau, the two-time U.S. Open champion who recently submitted his paperwork, earning Category 1 membership status.
body: McGinley’s concern focuses less on the immediate 2027 season and more on the long-term viability for players who stayed loyal to the traditional tours. In an interview with Sky Sports reported by Yahoo Sports, the Ryder Cup captain highlighted the sheer volume of talent returning. “Because you’ve got 30 really world-class players coming back to play on the DP World Tour next year from LIV, and they’re probably going to take 20 or 30 of the 100 cards that are available,” McGinley said. Current members are left with far fewer chances to keep their status for the upcoming year based on this math.

The return of high-profile names brings a complex mix of visibility and competition. While Rory McIlroy has suggested that the attention these players bring is a net positive for the sport, McGinley remains focused on the competitive pain points. He told Sky Sports that “The guys I feel sorry for are the guys not so much next year in 2027 on the DP World Tour, but 2028,” according to Golfmagic. The reasoning is straightforward: current members missed out on the rival circuit’s financial windfalls but now confront the fiercest battle for the limited remaining tour card spots.

articles.title: Wales beaten by 10-man Portugal as Neto scores but is sent off
articles.summary: Wales ended their Nations League group campaign with a 3-2 defeat against 10-man Portugal in Cardiff after Chelsea's Pedro Neto was sent off.
body: Although there was little riding on the contest, with Wales guaranteed a League A relegation/promotion play-off in March and Portugal having qualified for the quarter-finals, the two sides produced an entertaining spectacle.
Portugal skipper Bruno Fernandes blasted the opener after 11 minutes, but that was immediately wiped out by David Brooks' ninth goal for Wales.
Sorba Thomas broke free to put Wales ahead before the break, but again there was a quickfire response as Neto pounced to restore parity.

Substitute Carlos Forbs stroked Portugal ahead in the final quarter, and the visitors had to negotiate the final 16 minutes a player short after Neto was sent off after receiving two yellow cards in the space of two minutes.
